subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw own native gateway cost-budget enforcement, expose only a plugin/SDK admission contract for budget plugins, or rely on external provider/proxy spend controls?
rationale: The request crosses config defaults, provider/model dispatch, persistent ledger design, concurrency semantics, SDK hooks, and operator UX, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Native gateway budget policy
options.body: Add first-class per-agent/global budget windows with pre-dispatch admission, reservations, receipts, and status/doctor UX in core while leaving current users unlimited by default.

options.title: Plugin/SDK admission contract
options.body: Keep core lean by adding any missing atomic admission/receipt primitives to the plugin SDK and implement budget policy as an optional plugin.

options.title: External controls only
options.body: Document provider wallets or budget proxy patterns and close the core request unless a concrete missing OpenClaw API remains.

recommendation.title: Native gateway budget policy
recommendation.body: Add first-class per-agent/global budget windows with pre-dispatch admission, reservations, receipts, and status/doctor UX in core while leaving current users unlimited by default.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans the agent config, gateway usage, and embedded runner surfaces where this handle appears in recent central-path history.
